section_summary: This section contains Japanese budget schedules for 1932–35, embassy despatches on supplementary appropriations, and reports on national debt, taxation, military spending, and bond issues. A study of the Japanese money market examines its response to the 1933 American banking crisis and the risk that a rising yen would harm exports. File notes and intelligence reports point to related material on Japan’s wealth, foreign loans, and the developing 1934–35 budget.

subfiles.title: Japanese special-account budget schedules
subfiles.about: Schedules list revenue and expenditure for Japanese government departments and territorial special accounts.
subfiles.summary: The continuing budget schedules cover insurance, the Mint, monopoly operations, national loans, universities, rice control, railways, and colonial administrations. They record transfers among special accounts and ordinary and extraordinary spending for Korea, Taiwan, Kwantung, Karafuto, and the South Sea Islands.

subfiles.title: Division of Far Eastern Affairs note on the Japanese money market
subfiles.about: A note highlights Vice Consul Hutchinson’s forecast of the yen’s response to American inflation.
subfiles.summary: It warns that a rising yen could weaken exports while banks remain reluctant to lend.

subfiles.title: The Japanese Money Market and its Relation to the American Market
subfiles.about: The report analyzes Japanese money rates before and after the 1933 American banking crisis.
subfiles.summary: The report traces easing Japanese credit conditions through 1932 and the market’s reaction to the American bank closures and gold embargo. It discusses deposits, loans, the Bank of Japan’s open-market sales, exchange policy, and the risk to exports if the yen rises. Its appendix gives security values as of March 1, 1933, and the distribution of new capital in 1932.

subfiles.title: Division note on supplementary budget for 1933–34
subfiles.about: A note flags the navy arsenal’s ¥30 million share of a supplementary budget.
subfiles.summary: It summarizes Tokyo despatch No. 355 and its approximately ¥64 million budget.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 355: Supplementary Budget for 1933–34
subfiles.about: Grew transmits the supplementary budget passed by the Diet.
subfiles.summary: He notes that ¥30 million for the navy arsenal is nearly half the total and connects the claim to Japan’s withdrawal from the League of Nations. Other large claims fund disaster relief.

subfiles.title: Supplementary Budget for 1933–34
subfiles.about: The enclosure itemizes ¥64,010,928 in supplementary revenue and expenditure.
subfiles.summary: The tables identify borrowing and Treasury transfers as major revenue sources. Expenditure includes Manchurian affairs, Hokkaido and other disaster relief, foreign exchange control, and ¥30 million for the navy arsenal. A final table identifies sums eligible for carryover.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 356: Supplementary Budgets for 1932–33
subfiles.about: Grew transmits three supplementary budget bills passed by the 64th Diet.
subfiles.summary: He says the bills complete 1932–33 appropriations, though calculating total expenditure remains difficult.

subfiles.title: Special Account Supplementary Budget, February 1933
subfiles.about: The schedule distributes loan proceeds and increases navy arsenal and overseas-account funds.
subfiles.summary: It assigns ¥40.1 million in loans among general, Korean, and Kwantung accounts.

subfiles.title: General Account Supplementary Budget, March 1933
subfiles.about: The schedule lists additional ordinary and extraordinary appropriations.
subfiles.summary: Items include prisons, conferences, an embassy at Hsinking, disaster relief, and military allowances.

subfiles.title: Special Account Supplementary Budget, March 1933
subfiles.about: The enacted special-account supplement directs loans to the general account and funds territorial relief.
subfiles.summary: It records ¥28.4 million in loans plus Korean drought relief and Kwantung administrative aid.

subfiles.title: Government finance and gold shipment
subfiles.about: Report excerpts discuss budget-balancing bonds and a shipment of gold to the United States.
subfiles.summary: One excerpt states that the Diet passed a bond-issue bill to balance the 1933–34 budget. Another says Bank of Japan gold was shipped to meet government debt service and other expenses.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 367: Financial measures passed by the 64th Diet
subfiles.about: Grew transmits translated 1933–34 financial bills.
subfiles.summary: The surviving page begins a list of supplementary and extra budgets passed by the Diet.

subfiles.title: Special Account Supplementary Budget for 1933–34
subfiles.about: The enacted special-account supplement allocates funds among the Mint, debt redemption, loans, navy arsenal, universities, and overseas accounts.
subfiles.summary: Schedules include ¥65.3 million for national-loan redemption, ¥30 million for arsenal materials, flood repairs at Chiba Medical University, and exchange and rice-export controls in territorial accounts. The final table explains carryover expenditures.

subfiles.title: General Account Supplementary Budget for 1933–34
subfiles.about: The supplement appropriates ¥6,309,734, chiefly for Sanriku earthquake relief.
subfiles.summary: Loans fund debt amortization and ¥6.12 million in relief expenditure.

subfiles.title: Imperial Universities supplementary account
subfiles.about: A university account funds investigation of the Sanriku earthquake.
subfiles.summary: It transfers ¥10,000 to Tokyo Imperial University for disaster research.

subfiles.title: File note for Tokyo telegram No. 101
subfiles.about: The note points to Japan’s views before international monetary and economic talks.
subfiles.summary: It cross-references telegram No. 101 on money, credit, and the London conference.

subfiles.title: Tokyo telegram No. 101 on preliminary economic talks
subfiles.about: The telegram describes anticipated Japanese positions on political and economic questions.
subfiles.summary: It discusses a consultative pact, disarmament, gold and currency stabilization, tariffs, and trade. Japanese officials favor cooperation that serves national interests and seek credits or exchange assistance before stabilizing the yen.

subfiles.title: Government finances: national debt at March 31, 1933
subfiles.about: A report gives Japan’s national debt and outstanding short-term obligations.
subfiles.summary: It puts national debt at ¥7.054 billion, up ¥866.6 million during the year.

subfiles.title: File note on Takahashi’s proposed tax increases
subfiles.about: The note cross-references a despatch on financing increased 1934 expenditures.
subfiles.summary: Takahashi reportedly advocates raising some taxes because spending cannot be reduced.

subfiles.title: Government finance: 1934 budget and Deposits Bureau
subfiles.about: The excerpt discusses proposed tax increases and Deposits Bureau profits.
subfiles.summary: Most reported bureau profit came from foreign exchange gains on deposits held abroad.

subfiles.title: Division note on Japan’s national wealth
subfiles.about: The note summarizes a military attaché report estimating Japan’s national wealth.
subfiles.summary: It cites ¥110 billion in 1930 and explains how a changed calculation affects comparison with 1924.

subfiles.title: Military Intelligence Division distribution sheet
subfiles.about: The sheet lists War Department and other offices for distribution.
subfiles.summary: It provides routing options for information, filing, and return.

subfiles.title: Military attaché report on Japan’s national wealth
subfiles.about: A damaged report page tabulates Japanese national wealth.
subfiles.summary: The legible material includes a public-finance heading and wealth figures in millions of yen.

subfiles.title: Division note on despatch No. 454
subfiles.about: The note flags Embassy proposals for the 1934–35 budget.
subfiles.summary: It recommends reading the full June 30 despatch.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 454: Discussion of Budget for 1934–35
subfiles.about: Grew examines military demands, revenue limits, tax proposals, and cabinet politics during preparation of the 1934–35 budget.
subfiles.summary: Army and navy demands threaten to increase an already large budget while revenue remains substantially lower than expenditure. Takahashi considers tax increases and reductions in rural relief and Manchurian spending. The despatch also describes disputes over who would bear new taxes and the possible political consequences.

subfiles.title: Duplicate supplementary-budget table
subfiles.about: A repeated table page lists final extraordinary expenditures and carryover provisions.
subfiles.summary: It duplicates the figures and opening Table C material on page 273.

subfiles.title: File note for despatch No. 459
subfiles.about: The note cross-references cabinet discussion of the 1934–35 budget.
subfiles.summary: It says the next budget may equal the current year’s.

subfiles.title: File note for despatch No. 490
subfiles.about: The note cross-references continuing work on the 1934–35 budget.
subfiles.summary: It states that few developments can yet be reported.

subfiles.title: File note on Clarence E. Bosworth’s inquiry
subfiles.about: The note points to a request for information on Japan’s external loans.
subfiles.summary: It cross-references Bosworth’s letter in another file.

subfiles.title: File note on departmental budget estimates
subfiles.about: The note cross-references a report on the timetable for 1934–35 estimates.
subfiles.summary: Departments were asked to submit estimates by July 31, 1933.

subfiles.title: Military intelligence note on Japan’s public debt
subfiles.about: A damaged intelligence note reports Japanese public debt and Treasury bills.
subfiles.summary: It cites a Japan Chronicle report; several figures are illegible in the OCR.

subfiles.title: File note for despatch No. 541
subfiles.about: The note points to an expectation of higher national revenues next year.
subfiles.summary: It cross-references despatch No. 541.

subfiles.title: Government finance: budget and departmental requests
subfiles.about: A damaged report discusses projected revenue and requests for military and communications spending.
subfiles.summary: The legible text anticipates increased revenue but continued pressure from army, navy, and communications programs.

subfiles.title: Conclusion of despatch No. 454
subfiles.about: The final page of the June 30 budget discussion assesses Takahashi’s position.
subfiles.summary: Grew expects further reporting after ministries submit their estimates.

subfiles.title: File note on Tokyo municipal bonds in France
subfiles.about: The note cross-references French efforts to secure service on Tokyo’s 1912 bonds.
subfiles.summary: It refers to French court decisions and ambassadorial representations.

subfiles.title: French report on Tokyo bond service
subfiles.about: The excerpt discusses French demands that Tokyo resume service on its bond issue.
subfiles.summary: It says the city continued servicing English and American tranches while the French ambassador pressed for compliance with French court rulings.

subfiles.title: Division note on the draft 1934–35 budget
subfiles.about: The note recommends despatch No. 603 and summarizes its budget findings.
subfiles.summary: It says Takahashi’s proposed ceiling rose under military pressure to about ¥2.111 billion. Changes to the accounting of communications enterprises make a simple comparison with the previous budget misleading.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 603: Budget Agreement
subfiles.about: Grew reports the cabinet’s agreement on Japan’s 1934–35 budget.
subfiles.summary: The proposed budget totals ¥2.111537 billion after ministries initially sought more than ¥2.8 billion. Tables show departmental allocations, with army and navy spending prominent. Grew describes reduced rural relief, the effect of separate communications accounts, and planned financing through ¥785.335 million in bond issues, which would increase national debt.
